_about: Owner: Tour 1 writer (tours/life-of-a-chat-request). Terms of the request path that are not in core.json.

engine-core-request.short: The request object that the front end sends to the engine core. It is a msgspec struct with the token ids, the sampling parameters and the arrival time.
engine-core-request.long: Made by InputProcessor.process_inputs ({{cite vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py:538-555}}). Sent as msgpack over ZMQ.

engine-core-outputs.short: The message that the engine core sends back after a step. It holds one EngineCoreOutput (new token ids, finish reason) per request, plus scheduler stats.

scheduler-output.short: The plan of one engine step: which requests run, how many tokens each gets, and which KV blocks they use. The scheduler gives it to the executor.

request-output.short: The result object that AsyncLLM gives to the API server: new text, new token ids and a finished flag. In streaming mode it holds only the new part.

request-output-collector.short: A one-slot queue per request in the front end. The output handler puts RequestOutputs in it, and generate() takes them out. It merges outputs when the reader is slow.

output-processor.short: The front-end object that turns EngineCoreOutputs into RequestOutputs. It detokenizes, checks stop strings and computes the request metrics.

input-processor.short: The front-end object that checks a rendered prompt and its sampling parameters and makes an EngineCoreRequest.

busy-loop.short: The main loop of the engine core process. It takes new requests from the input queue, runs one engine step, and puts the outputs into the output queue.

async-scheduling.short: The engine core schedules and starts step k+1 before it waits for the result of step k. So CPU work overlaps with GPU work. It is on by default.

batch-queue.short: A short queue of started engine steps in the engine core. Its size is max_concurrent_batches: 2 on one GPU with async scheduling and Model Runner V2.

output-placeholder.short: A count of tokens that are in flight: a started step will sample them, but the scheduler does not have them yet. The async scheduler uses it to plan the next step of a request.
output-placeholder.long: num_output_placeholders: added at schedule time ({{cite vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:45-47}}), removed when the token arrives ({{cite vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:71-73}}).

incremental-detokenization.short: Turning token ids into text one token at a time, so each new token gives the next piece of text. vLLM uses the DecodeStream of the tokenizers library.
